_comment: virp-lab device template. Rendered to /run/virp/devices.json at daemon start by deploy/render-devices.sh, which substitutes ${...} placeholders from /etc/virp/autopilot.env (root-only). The template itself carries NO credentials for the API devices. HARD EXCLUSIONS apply: the daemon refuses to load any config containing a blocked address (see virp_config_blocked_address in virp_onode.c) — do not name them here, even in a comment, or the render output will be refused at startup.
_socket_allowlist_policy: DELIBERATE (2026-07-30): uid 0 is EXCLUDED. The allowlist is the daemon's own uid (rendered from ${VIRP_UID}) plus 1000, the interactive operator — the same policy CT 211 has always run. The autopilot runs as User=virp, i.e. the daemon's own service account (nologin, no sudo, cannot read /etc/virp/autopilot.env). A SEPARATE unprivileged uid was tried and rejected: verifying an observation requires the O-Key because VIRP signs with symmetric HMAC, and virp_key_load_file REFUSES a key with group read ("insecure mode 0640"), so a second account could only verify by weakening key hygiene or duplicating the key on disk. Verifier and signer cannot be separated until the daemon exposes a verify action; see DEPLOYED.md "socket allowlist policy".
_socket_allowlist_backup_note: ${VIRP_BACKUP_UID} is `virp-backup`, the config-backup runbook's dedicated identity (2026-07-30). It is a CLIENT-only uid: no key or credential group membership, socket reach granted by ACL (deploy/config-backup-access.sh), and it does NOT verify observations — it stores signed bytes for key holders to verify. This does not contradict the verifier-needs-the-key finding above: the runbook is a submitter, not a verifier.
_socket_allowlist_evidence_note: ${VIRP_EVIDENCE_UID} is `virp-evidence`, the compliance-evidence collector's dedicated identity (2026-07-30). Same CLIENT-only shape as virp-backup and, deliberately, a SEPARATE account from it: each automation owns its own identity and its own evidence tree, so a compromise of one runbook does not reach the other's evidence. It is read-only even within the GREEN set — it submits nothing but `vtysh -c "show ..."` reads (enforced locally as well as at the gate, because its item list is operator-editable). Verification is done afterwards by virp-evidence-report, which runs as a key holder.
_socket_allowlist_netclaw_note: ${VIRP_NETCLAW_UID} is `virp-netclaw`, the remote requester identity for netclaw (10.0.30.30), added 2026-08-09. Same CLIENT-only shape as virp-backup / virp-evidence: no key or credential group membership, socket reach granted by ACL (deploy/netclaw-access.sh, re-applied each start by the 52-netclaw drop-in). The uid is presented by the sshd child serving netclaw's streamlocal forward — the account is restrict-ed to that single capability (root-owned authorized_keys, from= pinned, no shell/PTY/TCP forwards) — so SO_PEERCRED identifies an authenticated remote requester, never a relay. It submits and cannot verify (no O-Key) and cannot approve (no approver secret on netclaw). Its effective ceiling is pinned to GREEN by socket_uid_tier_ceilings below, so YELLOW and RED are proposal-only for this uid — and unappliable, since it holds no approver key.
_socket_allowlist_broker_note: ${VIRP_BROKER_UID} is `virp-broker`, the Stage 1 intent-broker's dedicated identity (broker/virp_broker.py), added to the allowlist 2026-08-09 — until then the broker had a socket ACL but every forward would have been refused at the peercred gate, and none was ever logged. NOTE: Stage 1 is otherwise still INERT — the broker binds 127.0.0.1 only (IPAddressDeny=any beyond loopback in its unit), there is no mTLS, and no firewall pinhole reaches it. A working socket path does NOT mean a working broker: the VLAN bind, mTLS, and the pinhole remain separate, later, operator steps.
_socket_uid_tier_ceilings_note: Per-uid tier ceilings (2026-08-09). A uid listed here has its effective gate ceiling TIGHTENED to the named tier and can NEVER raise the node-wide gate_max_tier. ${VIRP_NETCLAW_UID} (virp-netclaw, the remote netclaw requester) is pinned to GREEN: reads auto-execute, while YELLOW and RED both become proposal-only for it — local operators (uid 1000) and the autopilot keep the node-wide YELLOW ceiling. This is what makes the remote AI path read-only-by-default without lowering the whole node. Enforced in onode_execute_obs_ex via onode_effective_max_tier, on BOTH the single and batch execute paths; the connecting uid is SO_PEERCRED, not client-asserted.
_socket_uid_tier_ceilings_note_2026_09_0: 999/1000/994 pinned to green when SW-3850 joined the fleet (2026-09-05). Before this they carried NO ceiling and so inherited the node-wide gate_max_tier, which is YELLOW — meaning the autopilot could auto-execute show running-config, show tech-support and clear counters against the switch that carries the colo. There is no per-device tier cap in this daemon; the only knobs are the node-wide gate_max_tier and this per-uid map, so protecting one device means capping the identities fleet-wide. MEASURED COST before applying it, 3 days of journal on this node: 319 YELLOW decisions, 313 of them already blocked at uid 997 (which has held a green ceiling all along), and exactly 3 allowed — all uid 999, all `vtysh -c "show running-config"` auto-executed against clab-frr-ospf-frr1. Those three now file a PROPOSAL instead of executing, which is a queue for a human, not a loss. virp-config-backup runs as uid 997 and is unaffected. uid 1000 and 994 executed no YELLOW at all in that window, so their caps cost nothing.
_socket_uid_action_allow_note: Per-uid ACTION allowlists (Item 8 mechanism 2026-08-11; config made mandatory Sep 1 review, Task 2). EVERY uid in socket_allowed_uids MUST have an entry here: the daemon treats an allowed-but-unmapped uid as unrestricted (shutdown included), so onode_start() now REFUSES TO RUN, naming the uid, when this object does not cover the allowlist — a forgotten entry is a boot failure, never a silent grant. Sets are the verbs each client actually sends, nothing more: ${VIRP_UID} is the daemon's own service account (autopilot, evidence report, camera submit-spool, virp-tool run as virp) and gets the full wire vocabulary EXCEPT shutdown — no client sends it and the unit stops on SIGTERM; 1000 is the interactive operator and keeps everything including shutdown; ${VIRP_BACKUP_UID} (autopilot/virp_config_backup.py) and ${VIRP_EVIDENCE_UID} (autopilot/virp_evidence.py) send exactly execute + chain_append — their reads go through the gate as execute, so execute cannot be withheld without ending collection; both are additionally read-only by classification (GREEN reads, per-uid GREEN ceiling); ${VIRP_NETCLAW_UID} gets what the installed virp-bridge-mcp.py on netclaw sends today (session_hello, session_bind, execute, chain_append — chain_append is type-narrowed to the federation triple for any mapped uid) and, pointedly, not shutdown, not list_fleet/health/chain_verify which that client never sends; ${VIRP_BROKER_UID} gets the broker's own relay allowlist (broker/virp_broker.py ALLOWED_ACTIONS). tests/test_template_uid_policy.py renders this file and asserts the coverage and the no-shutdown rule for the four service identities.
_socket_uid_netclaw_verbs_followup: FOLLOW-UP (2026-09-02, v0.2.1 deploy). ${VIRP_NETCLAW_UID} carries the verb set the RUNNING node has today — list_fleet, health, chain_verify, chain_append, execute — not the set this file previously proposed (session_hello, session_bind, execute, chain_append). The two sets are DISJOINT in four verbs: the proposal drops list_fleet/health/chain_verify and adds session_hello/session_bind. Reconciling them changes what a live remote client may send in BOTH directions and must be its own change, with virp-bridge-mcp.py on netclaw tested against it — not a side effect of a v0.2.1 correctness deploy. The chain_append TYPE policy below is unaffected: 30 days of this node's own traffic show uid 993 appending only fed_request/fed_observation/fed_outcome since 2026-08-11, so the fed_* triple is a no-op restatement of its live reach. "fed_error" is added 2026-09-03 and is NOT a restatement: it is the new type the bridge appends to close a request/outcome pair that died before an observation existed. Until this row is deployed the bridge's error path is refused at the type policy and falls back to leaving the pair open, which is the pre-2026-09-03 behaviour — so the daemon and this row must land together, and the bridge is safe to deploy ahead of both.
_socket_uid_chain_append_types_note: Per-uid chain_append TYPE policy (v0.2.1). A uid that may chain_append is restricted to exactly these artifact types; any allowlisted uid whose action set includes chain_append MUST appear here or the daemon refuses to start naming the uid. This REPLACES the v0.2.0 inference that any action-mapped uid was a federated principal narrowed to fed_* — which silently refused the local service accounts' real appends. The netclaw bridge's fed_* reach is now one row here, not a code path. Types use the 16-byte-truncated spellings the wire delivers (comparator_verdict -> comparator_verd, chainwalk_summary -> chainwalk_summa). Broker is absent because its relay allowlist has no chain_append.
_socket_uid_deployed_state_note: ${VIRP_UID} gains 'evidence_item' (2026-09-02) so the deployed-state reporter (tools/state/deployed-state.sh, unit virp-deployed-state.service) can land its deployed_state/1 document as a real BODY rather than a commitment-only hash that every reader would correctly grade UNVERIFIABLE. It is a deliberate, small widening and it is written here rather than reused from another identity: 'observation' WITH a body needs a GATE 3 signature under the O-Key the reporter does not hold, and a purpose-built 'deployed_state' type would mean editing the fixed C array in virp_chain_type_is_external_allowed(), rebuilding and redeploying every node. ${VIRP_UID} is the node's OWN service account and a deployed-state document is the node's self-report, which is why it is the right identity here rather than virp-evidence's — each automation owning its own identity is the standing policy, and borrowing the evidence collector's would break it. ${VIRP_UID} could already append 'observation', the type GATE 3 guards most strictly, so this adds a plain-JSON evidence body to an account that is strictly more privileged than virp-evidence, which has held exactly this type since 2026-07-30. NOT YET ON ANY BOX: this row lands at the next deploy.
_evidence_required_note: Evidence-required execution (Sep 1 review, Task 5). true (the daemon's compiled-in default, restated here so the posture is visible in the rendered config): every execution the gate admits is preceded by a durable gate_intent chain entry — device, command, tier, uid, v2 session, proposal — committed BEFORE the driver is dispatched; if that append fails (chain read-only, disk full, chain absent) the operation is REFUSED with a signed ERROR observation citing evidence-unavailable and nothing reaches the device. The gate_execution / outcome entry written afterwards links back to the intent by chain_entry_hash; a daemon that dies between the two leaves an intent with no closer, which `virp chain-verify` and report/verify.py report as an OPEN EXECUTION (reconcile against the target) and never as a broken chain. Requires the trust chain (-c/-C in the unit); the daemon refuses to START with evidence required and no usable chain. Set to false ONLY to restore the pre-Task-5 record-after-the-fact posture — the daemon then logs a WARNING on every dispatch that it ran without a durable record. Must be a JSON boolean: any other value is logged and ignored (default stays true).

devices._comment: Wazuh manager. protected_agents names the agents the driver refuses to touch at ANY tier — enforced in wazuh_execute() and returned as VIRP_TIER_BLACK by the gate hook, so the refusal files no proposal and no approval reaches it. Ids compare numerically, so "004" and 4 are one agent. Do NOT rely on the API credential's RBAC for this: Wazuh denies at resource level by returning HTTP 200 with the agent simply absent from affected_items, which is indistinguishable from the agent not existing.
devices._tls_note: The driver verifies the certificate by default. A stock Wazuh manager presents a self-signed cert whose only SAN is DNS:localhost, so addressing it by IP fails hostname verification even with that cert trusted as a CA. Fix the CERTIFICATE (reissue with an IP or DNS SAN via wazuh-certs-tool.sh) and point VIRP_CA_BUNDLE at its signer. The VIRP_WAZUH_INSECURE drop-in disables verification entirely and is a lab-only last resort.
devices._protected_agents_status: protected_agents is DELIBERATELY UNSET for this device (2026-09-02). The ids previously listed here, 004 and 313, are the HOME Wazuh manager's agent ids. Read back from the colo manager at 10.0.20.10 through the gate as a GREEN "GET /agents", it has seven agents and neither id is among them: 000 wazuh, 001 pve1, 006 librenms, 007 pbs, 008 thirdlevel-ai-web, 009 ironclaw-onode, 011 netclaw. Listing ids that do not exist protects nothing and reads as protection that is not there, so the running node's omission is kept. Decide which of the seven real ids belong on the never-class list and set them in their own change.

devices._comment: SW-3850 — the colo Catalyst 3850 stack. Added 2026-09-05 for the TACACS+ accounting work: the gate needs a GREEN observation of a command so it can be paired against the switch's own accounting record of the same command. READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION, in two ways that are both deliberate. (1) No "enable" credential: aiops-svc is privilege 15 and lands at '#', and the no-enable refusal in virp_onode_prod.c is cisco_asa-only, so omitting it costs nothing and leaves the gate with no enable secret to hold. The password rides ${SWITCH_PASS}, a placeholder render-devices.sh already carries for "cat3850-lab (10.0.10.2)" — this exact switch — so no change to the render script is needed; the value goes in autopilot.env, never in this file, which is 0644. (2) vendor cisco_iosxe shares driver_cisco's functions and gate table with cisco_ios but is a distinct vendor so the gate can address IOS-XE independently and the journal says which variant a command hit. NOTE the node-wide gate_max_tier here is YELLOW and uids 999/1000/994 carry no per-uid ceiling, so absent a ceiling decision the autopilot may auto-execute YELLOW against this switch — which on this box includes show running-config, show tech-support and clear counters.

Zammad, READ-ONLY half. Two entries point at the same host and differ in exactly two things: the token behind them and write_ops_allow. This one names NO write operation, so zammad_execute refuses every typed write against it in the driver, before the connection is touched — it does not rely on Zammad returning 403, because a token-permission change on the far side would then silently become a policy change here.
devices._tls_note: The driver always uses https and always verifies; there is no insecure flag and no CA-bundle override. The certificate for 10.0.40.20 (CN zammad.thirdlevel.ai) carries an iPAddress SAN, which is why addressing by IP validates. Rotating to a certificate without that SAN means addressing by name instead, not disabling verification.

devices._comment: Zammad, READ-WRITE half. The ONLY device in this file carrying write_ops_allow. The value is an exact op-id allowlist — no prefixes, no wildcards, no 'all' spelling exists. Adding a second operation here is a deliberate act that should come with its own review, because the driver will then permit it on this device.
devices._tier_note: ticket.article.create classifies YELLOW. The node-wide ceiling is YELLOW so a local operator executes it directly; uid 993 (virp-netclaw) carries a GREEN ceiling in socket_uid_tier_ceilings, so for the remote requester the same command is proposal-only and cannot be self-applied (it holds no approver key). Demoting the row to GREEN would hand the write to the remote path silently.

devices._comment: Proxmox Backup Server — typed-operation driver. The command a caller submits is NOT an API path: it is a canonical typed operation, `pbs op=<operation.id> [key=value ...]`, and the driver derives method and URL from a static table. See docs/DRIVER-TYPED-OPS.md.
devices._tls_note: tls_fingerprint is the SHA-256 fingerprint of the PBS leaf certificate and is MANDATORY: the driver refuses to connect without it and the daemon refuses to LOAD this device without it. There is deliberately no verify_tls boolean here and no insecure mode in the driver — a boolean has a value meaning 'do not check', a fingerprint does not. Rotating the PBS certificate is therefore a config change here; that is the intended cost.
devices._datastore_note: datastore_allow is the exact set of datastore names accepted for op=backup.snapshots.list. The grammar constrains the SHAPE of the store parameter; this constrains its VALUE. The gate hook receives no device context, so this check lives in the driver — see the shape-vs-value split in tests/test_driver_pbs_gate.c.

devices._comment: IronClaw colo fleet stage 1. PAN-OS op mode has full read access — no enable mode exists, so the LAB_ENABLE placeholder (dollar-brace form) must NOT be named on this row (render policy: a placeholder named here loads a secret into the daemon that no driver will ever read).

IronClaw colo fleet stage 1. The only stage-1 row with enable: the ASA driver enters (and re-enters) enable mode. ssh_legacy is deliberately NOT set — verified 2026-08-09 from this node that the driver's default algorithm set negotiates with this unit (kex diffie-hellman-group14-sha1, hostkey ssh-rsa, cipher aes256-ctr; the ASA offers nothing newer and all three are in the default preference list).

IronClaw colo fleet stage 1. JunOS has a flat privilege model — no enable. IronClaw's own inventory carries ssh_legacy=true for this device, but that is stale: the unit runs OpenSSH 6.9 and offers ecdh-sha2-nistp256, first in the juniper driver's default kex list (verified 2026-08-09 from this node), so it is imported without ssh_legacy.
